<img class="tool-icon" src="../../../../images/tekla/tools/usectioncutter.svg" alt="" width="48" height="48" style="display:block;margin:0 0 1rem;background:#fff;border-radius:8px;padding:4px" />

{{% callout type="info" %}}
**Where to find it:** Applications & Components → Comma → `uSectionCutter`
{{% /callout %}}

Cuts a section line/plane through picked parts and draws the resulting intersection. Runs as a one-shot tool: click it once, then keep picking — it stays open until you press <kbd>Esc</kbd>.

**How to use:**

1.  Click the icon in the catalog (or press Apply from its dialog).
2.  Choose a **Mode**: *Line + Z* (pick 2 points, cuts vertically through the active view's own orientation), *Plane (3 points)* (pick 3 points directly), or *Face* (pick a face on a part — its own plane is used).
3.  Line + Z and Plane mode both show a live grey line following the cursor while picking, the same rubber-band preview Tekla's own native commands use — Face mode does not (it picks a face directly, not points).
4.  Pick the parts to cut (you can pick several at once, then confirm).
5.  The cut repeats immediately for another line/plane/face — press Esc when done.

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Offset** | Shifts the cutting plane along its own normal before intersecting (0 = exactly as picked). |
| **Line color** | Colour of the drawn cut lines (construction-object mode only). |
| **Line type** | Solid / Dashed / Slashed / Dash dotted / Dotted (construction-object mode only — a reference DXF has no line-type table, so that mode always exports a continuous line regardless of this setting). |
| **Add points** | Also marks every vertex of the cut with a construction point. |
| **Orient to XY** | Off by default (cut geometry stays at its real 3D model location). On: re-orients the cross-section into the cutting plane's own local 2D coordinates and moves it to the global origin (0,0,0) on the XY plane — useful for pulling a cross-section out to look at flat, on its own, instead of wherever in 3D it was actually cut. Applies to both Creation methods below. Note: every cut made with this on lands at the same origin, so repeated cuts will overlap there rather than spread out through the model. |
| **Creation method** | *Construction object* (default): the cut is inserted as plain construction lines/points, same as the native "Add construction line" tool. *Reference DXF*: the same cut geometry is written to a small DXF file and inserted as a reference model instead — useful if you want the result to sit in its own toggleable layer rather than mixed in with ordinary construction objects. The DXF file is saved in a `uSectionCutter` subfolder inside the model's own folder, one file per cut. |

<blockquote class="page-note"><strong>Note:</strong> Line + Z mode follows the active <strong>view's</strong> orientation, not a work plane set via the Cpl command — for a plane that follows a custom work plane, use Plane (3 points) mode instead.</blockquote>
